newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices rise on spectre of more cold in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices rise on spectre of more cold in U.S.

text.p: Oil prices rose on Wednesday as a rally gained support from latest forecasts of a second cold snap in the U.S prolonging cold temperatures into next week.
Bearish U.S. stocks data showing a sharp rise in heating oil inventories in the world's leading energy consuming nation tried but failed to bring prices lower.
"The forecast of cold weather beat the inventories," said one oil trader.
In London, February futures for world marker crude Brent Blend, rose to the day's high of $24.80 a barrel, up 21 cents.

Oil prices started the year with a strong rally on the back of freezing weather across Europe, which boosted gas oil (used in Europe for heating purposes) values and put a firm floor under crude oil prices.
Front-month Brent rose steadily from the beginning of January, gaining nearly $1 a barrel despite the resumption of Iraqi crude oil exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal three weeks ago.

The weather card was prominent again on Wednesday. Reports of temperaturs of eight to 15 degrees below normal for the U.S midcontinent and two degrees below normal in the Northeast next week, shouldered aside concerns over U.S inventory data.
The information published on Wednesday showed a 2.94 million barrel build in distillates stocks (which include heating oil) last week.
The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) led the London market higher as U.S dealers digested the bearish distillates stocks data but then put their faith in colder weather.
The rise in crude prices also gained some support from news that U.S crude oil stocks held in primary storage fell 9.47 million barrels in the week ending January 3.
However, a cautionary note was made by brokers at GNI and Prudential Bache in London said the information should be seen in the context of end of year tax considerations.

"The crude draw is less positive than the headline figure for a couple of reasons. First, end of year tax considerations have played a role, and there have been problems with the weather conditions in the U.S. Gulf, which have disrupted loadings," GNI said.

Despite weekly fluctuations in U.S. stock levels, inventories are overall lower than year-ago levels and low industry stocks in consuming countries were the main reason for pushing oil prices to a near six-year high in October last year.

The Iraqi crude which started flowing into the market on December 16 under the U.N. limited oil sales deal has been absorbed by a tight winter market. U.N. sources said on Tuesday Iraqi exports would peak in late February/ early March to around 618,000 barrels per day (bpd).

Iraq has been under U.N. sanctions since its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Under the partial sales plan, Baghdad will be allowed to export $2 billion worth of crude oil over six months to pay for food and medicines.
